title: NACOSTI Strengthens Research Ethics and Integrity Capacity through Five-day Training
excerpt: A national training programme brought together research and ethics professionals to strengthen responsible research practice in Kenya.
details: The five-day programme covered research governance, ethics review, informed consent, vulnerable populations, research integrity and security, community engagement, and institutional review procedures. Sessions also considered emerging issues such as open science, synthetic biology, big data, and artificial intelligence.

title: Africa Rallies to Inspire Next-Generation Nuclear Scientists
excerpt: A regional gathering focused on introducing young people to nuclear science and expanding Africa's future scientific workforce.
details: The meeting advanced IAEA project RAF0065, which supports science outreach across African member states. Delegates discussed early exposure for secondary-school students, mentorship, teacher development, and wider participation by women and young people, while highlighting peaceful applications including healthcare, agriculture, and water management.

title: PPB Regulatory Notice: Concurrent Submission Pilot Framework for Clinical Trial Applications
excerpt: A Pharmacy and Poisons Board pilot allows clinical-trial applications to move through regulatory and ethics review in parallel.
details: Applicants in the pilot submit the same complete application to the PPB and a participating ethics committee within five working days. The initial participating committees are KEMRI SERU and MTRH IREC. Ethics approval remains required before the PPB can issue final authorization.

title: IAEA Regional Meeting on Climate, Land-Use, Energy and Water Systems Opens in Nairobi
excerpt: Nairobi hosted an African regional meeting on coordinated planning across climate, land use, energy, and water systems.
details: Convened by NACOSTI with EPRA and the IAEA under AFRA, the five-day meeting brought together delegates from 20 African countries. Participants worked on integrated planning scenarios, modelling approaches, data-sharing principles, and a priority matrix and action plan to guide future regional cooperation.

title: Kenya Aligns Partners for STRI4Society 2026
excerpt: Government, academic, industry, and development partners met to strengthen collaboration ahead of STRI4Society Week.
details: The Nairobi engagement focused on aligning partners and mobilizing support to connect research with national development priorities. STRI4Society Week was planned for 18–22 May 2026 at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre, with policy discussions, innovation exhibitions, and youth-focused activities.

title: Regional Science Collaboration in Focus as NACOSTI Hosts AFRA Stakeholders
excerpt: AFRA project partners met to review progress and strengthen regional cooperation in nuclear science and technology.
details: The stakeholder meeting brought together policymakers, researchers, academic institutions, and partners to discuss achievements, implementation challenges, and next steps. Discussions highlighted shared capacity building and peaceful nuclear-science applications in areas such as health, agriculture, water resources, and environmental management.

title: Science and Innovation Take Centre Stage as Kenya Launches New Blueprint
excerpt: Kenya launched a blueprint intended to better coordinate the national research and innovation ecosystem.
details: The framework sets out priorities including stronger research infrastructure, funding mechanisms, commercialization of research, and links between academia and industry. It is designed to align research with national development goals and encourage collaboration among public institutions, researchers, and the private sector.

title: NACOSTI Supports National Tree Growing Campaign with a Tree Planting Exercise
excerpt: NACOSTI staff and local partners took part in a tree-growing activity at the University of Nairobi's Upper Kabete campus.
details: The exercise supported national efforts to restore forest cover and promote environmental sustainability. Participants planted suitable indigenous species and highlighted how conservation, research, and community participation can contribute to climate resilience, biodiversity, and responsible land management.

title: NACOSTI Hosts Bio-KE Project Advisory Board Meeting
excerpt: Stakeholders convened to shape a national education and policy framework for a sustainable bioeconomy.
details: The Bio-KE forum explored how Kenya can build on its biodiversity, agriculture, and research capacity to support bio-based innovation. Discussions included policy alignment, education, research investment, turning organic waste into value, and stronger cooperation between government, academia, and industry.
